text:
Priya: quick thread on immediate revocation for service tokens — saw a support case where a disabled key was still accepted for ~45s.
Jonas: right now gateway caches actor assertions for 2m to keep authz lookups cheap.
Mei: that explains it. customer clicked disable in console, but gateway reply was cached.
Raj: two approaches: (A) make gateway check the authz service on every request (expensive), (B) keep cache but add a 'revocation push' path to evict entries.
Priya: push seems better but we need to think about ordering, replay, and scale.
Jonas: design idea: each authz update emits a narrow-scoped event: {kind: "evict", key: "apiKey:K234", scope: "svc:payments", rev: 12345, ts: 1766667770}. edges subscribe.
Mei: what about re-create races? if a key is revoked then re-created immediately, we might evict legitimate new key.
Raj: include a fingerprint (creation_ts or a non-reused id). eviction only removes cache entries matching fingerprint.
Priya: good. also we can include a small TTL on edge side (like 15s) so push covers immediate cases and TTL handles missed messages.
Jonas: tradeoffs: TTL 15s reduces backend QPS vs TTL 120s. with push we add complexity around connections and auth for the push channel.
Mei: security concern: ensure invalidation messages are authenticated — HMAC + key rotation for the change-proxy -> edge channel.
infra-bot: NOTE: publish-subscribe endpoints must rotate signing keys every 30d. See policy: https://redwood.internal/policies/pubsub-signing
Raj: we also need monotonic rev numbers per subject so edges can ignore stale invalidations. e.g., if evict rev=10 arrives then later rev=9, ignore.
Priya: perf question: how many evicts/min in worst-case? if an attacker floods revoke API, we could end up sending N evicts to many edges.
Jonas: mitigation: rate-limit administrative revokes, bulk-change flows should emit batch deltas rather than per-actor events. also we can collapse events by subject for a short debounce window.
Mei: for multi-tenant routing: some customers want sub-second revocation SLA. propose two modes: standard (<=30s) and enterprise immediate (<=1s) with dedicated push channels per-tenant.
Raj: dedicated channels cost more but make sense for high-security tenants. we should expose this as a per-org flag.
Priya: clients: API key users might be scripts that don't support refresh. forcing short lived keys is breaking. so prefer push + fingerprint approach.
Jonas: implementation plan: (1) change-proxy: emit signed evict events with subject+fingerprint+rev, (2) edge: persistent consumer with backpressure, compare rev+fingerprint, evict matching cache entry, (3) fallback: if consumer disconnected, edge falls back to TTL and periodic delta-sync.
Mei: operational plan: add telemetry on evict success/failure rates, queue lag, and a dashboard for deviation from SLA.
infra-bot: REMINDER: add integration tests for replay, ordering, and signature verification.
Priya: one more thought: role inheritance changes can touch thousands of actors; we must compute deltas at source and emit scoped evicts (avoid global invalidation).
Raj: yes, compute minimal delta and emit per-actor invalidations, or use a hierarchical event that edges can apply locally to compute changes if they store partial graph.
Jonas: prototype timeline: spike (2w) to build push PoC + perf harness (simulate 50k edges), then small rollout behind feature flag.
Mei: I'll draft the proposal for the spike and include attack/resilience scenarios.
Priya: great. assign owners: Jonas (push infra), Mei (security + tests), Raj (delta computation), Liza (docs & API docs).
Priya: thanks all — will follow up in the eng-security channel with the PR link in 48h. :rocket:
